summary: @servicetitan/startup-jest preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes an obfuscated bundle
details: The package's preinstall hook runs setup.mjs, which downloads the Bun runtime (bun-v1.3.13) from GitHub releases into a temp directory, extracts and chmods the Bun binary executable, and invokes it against a bundled sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a ~727 KB Bun-compiled CJS bundle obfuscated with a string-array rotator (WV8StW) and hex-identifier renaming, hiding all URLs, sinks, and control flow. setup.mjs itself uses obfuscator.io-style hex identifiers and per-function string-lookup objects to conceal its logic. The package presents as a jest CLI wrapper — its dist/index.js only exports a plain runJestCli — so there is no functional reason to fetch an alternate runtime or execute a 727 KB opaque payload at install time. The pattern is alternate-runtime dropping: shipping an opaque payload that only executes under a freshly-fetched non-default runtime bypasses Node-focused inspection and hands install-time code execution on the installer's machine to whatever math_init.js contains. The Bun runtime fetch is version-pinned to an official source, but the executed payload is author-supplied, unverified, obfuscated, and unrelated to the advertised jest-wrapper purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
